findings.claim: Immediate endpoint selection evidence is strongest for short-range pair kernels: pair_kernel_1.5 (endpoint_effects:9, integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (endpoint_effects:10, z 0.631, q 2.2e-5, fraction 1.0) and pair_kernel_3.5 (endpoint_effects:11, z 0.540, q 9.8e-5, fraction 1.0), with pair_kernel_5.0 weaker (endpoint_effects:12, z 0.319, q 3.7e-3) and pair_kernel_7.0 opposite in sign (endpoint_effects:13, z -0.485, q 1.5e-4). Branch-adjusted raw and adjusted correlations agree in sign and batch direction for the 1.5 and 2.5 kernels (branch_adjusted:163/164/240/241).

Descendant survival credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity. The only survival_enrichment_z entries with q below 0.5 are landmark_00_soft_mass (survival_effects:0, z 0.365, q 0.120), landmark_07_soft_mass (survival_effects:70, z 0.220, q 0.356), landmark_10_soft_mass (survival_effects:100, z 0.234, q 0.302), landmark_18_local_czz (survival_effects:186, z 0.217, q 0.302) and landmark_02_local_dz (survival_effects:23, z 0.206, q 0.356); several negative entries (survival_effects:46, 56, 96, 146, 156, 195) are also nominally significant. Because decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false, none of these can be presented as final affinity benefit.

The actual later-label calculation is unavailable: decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false, terminal metadata place terminal_index 99 at terminal_score_time 0.99 and terminal_state_time 1.0, outside the learning window [0.0,0.5] and the curve support [0.0,0.49]. Ancestral coverage is thin (lineage_support reports 349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 with fewer than 6), so last-record survival credit cannot be compared with final affinity benefit; that comparison is reported as unavailable.

Immediate selection evidence and descendant survival credit disagree in direction priority. The endpoint contrast favors short-range pair kernels (endpoint_effects:9-11) and penalizes pair_kernel_7.0 (endpoint_effects:13), whereas survival enrichment is positive for soft_mass at landmarks 00, 07 and 10 (survival_effects:0, 70, 100) and shows no significant pair-kernel survival effect. This disagreement is why pair-kernel direction should be prioritized over soft-mass direction in the immediate-selection reading, while the survival reading remains a separate, weaker credit signal.

Multiplicity-adjusted support and coverage rank coordinate hypotheses differently from point estimates alone. pair_kernel_1.5 and pair_kernel_2.5 retain q below 0.02 in both raw and adjusted covariance/correlation families (branch_adjusted:86, 87, 163, 164, 240, 241), while joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A have the smallest q values (branch_adjusted:228, 230, 305, 307) but are joint-motion diagnostics rather than local coordinate hypotheses. A concrete priority decision that differs from point-estimate ranking is to rank pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 above landmark_00_softmin and landmark_00_occupancy3 despite comparable point estimates, because the pair kernels have higher same-sign batch fractions (0.79-0.93) and lower q.

Independent-batch agreement supports the short-range pair-kernel direction: pair_kernel_1.5 and 2.5 have same_sign_batch_fraction 0.79-0.93 across 14 independent batches (branch_adjusted:163, 164, 240, 241), whereas pair_kernel_7.0 has negative whole-window means and lower same-sign fractions (branch_adjusted:167, 244). The counterexample that would weaken the proposed short-range pair-kernel direction is a batch in which pair_kernel_1.5 or 2.5 changes sign; the supplied same-sign fractions show that this occurs in roughly one to three of fourteen batches, so the direction is reproducible but not unanimous.

Local coordinate information must be separated from global pose and shape. The joint diagnostics show selection innovation is associated with native alignment (joint_diagnostics:1, q 2.2e-9) and teacher innovation-contrast alignment (joint_diagnostics:11, q 2.2e-9), while observed child score gain is negatively associated (joint_diagnostics:2, q 1.8e-7). The teacher contrast is predominantly internal (joint_diagnostics:14, mean 0.787) with atom participation fraction 0.384 (joint_diagnostics:15), so the region that adds information beyond common motion is the internal/local component, and the surrounding coordinates that should retain freedom are the global translation and rotation components (joint_diagnostics:12, 13). No adjustment beyond the supplied joint diagnostics is claimed.

The supplied continuous contrast functions for landmark_00 span the complete observed support [0.0,0.49] with observed_node_linear interpolation and no extrapolation. They show sign changes and rate changes: landmark_00_soft_mass rises from -0.366 to a peak near 1.64 and returns to -0.275 (continuous:0), while landmark_00_local_dx and local_dy change sign multiple times (continuous:1, 2). A constant rule would miss these sign changes; a time-conditioned rule using the observed-node interpolation is supported by the supplied fits, but the curve is a contrast, not an absolute reward target.

Curve fidelity is limited: curve_support reports relative_node_rmse between 0.386 and 0.931 for the audited curves, with strong_sign_conflict_nodes up to 15, and legendre_runtime_allowed is false for all audited entries. The selected_count is 24 under a rule requiring relative_rmse_le 0.35 and strong_sign_conflict_nodes_eq 0, so most audited curves fail the fidelity rule. This limits how strongly any time-conditioned rule can be justified from these curves.

Population-contrast changes and parent-child increment contrasts differ. Turnover accounting shows large positive edge_rate and turnover_residual_rate for landmark_00_soft_mass (turnover:1, 2), landmark_00_local_cxx (turnover:14), landmark_00_local_cyy (turnover:17), landmark_01_local_cyy (turnover:47), landmark_04_local_cxx (turnover:134), landmark_07_local_cxx (turnover:224), landmark_08_local_cxx (turnover:254), landmark_16_local_cyy (turnover:497), landmark_17_local_cxx (turnover:524) and landmark_19_local_cxx (turnover:584). The turnover residual is an accounting diagnostic that includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or atom velocity, so it cannot by itself establish within-path change versus changing cohort composition.

Parent-child increment contrasts are mostly not significant after multiplicity adjustment: landmark_00_softmin has a negative success-failure integrated rate (increment_effects:14, q 0.046) and landmark_00_occupancy3 a positive one (increment_effects:15, q 0.081), while shape_xx, shape_yy, shape_xz, pair_kernel_2.5, pair_kernel_7.0, landmark_03_occupancy5 and landmark_16_occupancy3 have q between 0.096 and 0.226 (increment_effects:3, 4, 7, 10, 13, 25, 63). The evidence therefore supports within-path change only weakly and does not cleanly separate it from changing cohort composition.

A testable coordinate intervention can be expressed with the registered pointcloud_delta_A edit: observable is the endpoint pointcloud reward R=tau*logsumexp(log_pi-rho_delta(q)/tau) with q the Hungarian mean squared endpoint distance; intended response is a change in the short-range pair-kernel contrast; target origin is the endpoint world coordinates; spatial scale is the pair-kernel shell radius (1.5-3.5 A); temporal scale is the learning window [0.0,0.5]. The discriminating failure condition is a batch in which pair_kernel_1.5 or 2.5 changes sign under the intervention. The permitted reward recipe that could express this is the endpoint pointcloud with pointcloud_delta_A in {0.5, 1.0, 2.0}; the temporal_teacher_blend recipe remains descriptive because no validated absolute contrast change is available at actual score nodes.

hypotheses.claim: Short-range pair-kernel contrast (1.5-3.5 A) is the most reproducible immediate-selection coordinate signal and would be the first hypothesis to test with a pointcloud_delta_A edit.

Soft-mass survival enrichment at landmarks 00, 07 and 10 is a recorded joint-head credit signal that may or may not correspond to final affinity benefit; it cannot be tested as an affinity hypothesis without decoded terminal labels.

The internal component of the teacher contrast, not the global translation or rotation component, carries the selection-innovation association; a hypothesis that local internal coordinates add information beyond common motion is supported by the joint diagnostics.

A time-conditioned contrast rule for landmark_00 may outperform a constant rule, but the low curve fidelity (relative_node_rmse up to 0.93, strong sign conflicts) makes this hypothesis weak and descriptive.

Large turnover residuals at landmark_00 and landmark_01 local coordinates may reflect score reclassification and parent weighting rather than within-path change; this remains an accounting hypothesis, not a causal selection effect.

Parent-child increment contrasts for landmark_00_softmin and landmark_00_occupancy3 are the only increment effects with q below 0.1, suggesting a weak within-path change hypothesis that requires independent-batch confirmation.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
Decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, so last-record credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term; pair-kernel and moment effects are diagnostic only.
